common_name: Duchess Blue and White Torenia (Compact Bicolor Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors and transplant after the last frost; performs well massed under trees or in shaded container plantings.

directions: Start seed indoors and transplant after the last frost. Duchess is a newer, extra-compact torenia series bred for a tidy mounded habit and heavy bud set, an improvement in uniformity over older wishbone flower strains. Duchess Blue and White produces crisp, two-tone violet-blue and white tubular flowers with the characteristic fused wishbone-shaped stamens, held just above neat foliage. It handles heat and humidity better than many older torenia selections and works well massed under trees or in shaded container plantings where few flowering annuals thrive.

common_name: Beacon Bright Red Impatiens (Downy-Mildew-Resistant Bedding Impatiens)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; consistent moisture is essential, as impatiens wilt quickly in dry soil.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost. Beacon was bred with strong resistance to Impatiens downy mildew, the disease that collapsed most Impatiens walleriana bedding plantings in North America and Europe starting around 2011, and it was recognized as an AAS Flower Award winner for restoring seed-grown impatiens as a dependable shade bedding choice. It keeps the classic mounded habit and abundant flat-faced flowers of traditional impatiens, here in a vivid bright red, and stays reliably full and floriferous through humid summers where older strains often thinned out and died.

common_name: Wizard Golden Coleus (Seed-Grown Chartreuse Foliage Coleus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; pinch out small flower spikes as they form to keep energy in foliage production.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost. The Wizard series was an early AAS-winning breakthrough in raising coleus reliably and uniformly from seed rather than cuttings, and it remains one of the most widely grown seed coleus lines. Wizard Golden bears bright chartreuse-gold leaves with a small maroon center blotch, brightening shaded beds and mixed containers all season on compact, well-branched plants. Pinching out the small blue flower spikes as they form keeps the plant's energy in foliage production and prevents legginess.

common_name: Riviera Sky Blue Lobelia (Compact Non-Trailing Edging Lobelia)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; shear plants back lightly after summer heat slows bloom to encourage a fall flush.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost. Riviera is a compact, mounding lobelia series (not trailing) bred for earlier bloom and better heat tolerance than older lobelia strains, though it still performs best where summers stay relatively cool. Riviera Sky Blue smothers itself in small, clear sky-blue flowers with a tiny white eye, forming a dense low carpet ideal for edging, rock gardens, and front-of-border plantings. Bloom often slows in peak summer heat; shearing plants back lightly encourages a strong flush of rebloom as temperatures moderate.
